info.text:
In 2022, US gas prices jumped 31%. Americans barely bought less.
Regular gas averaged $3.01/gal in 2021 and $3.95 in 2022, while US gasoline use fell less than 1% (EIA).
That's price elasticity: % change in amount bought divided by % change in price. Hypothetical: price +10%, gallons -1% = -0.1, inelastic, and the weekly bill rises from $40.00 to $43.56.
Cigarettes too: a 10% price rise cuts cigarettes smoked about 3-5%.
Sources: EIA retail gasoline prices and consumption data; National Cancer Institute Monograph 14; CDC.
News and education, not financial advice.
